obligations.note: retention.py:14 now skips a held payee only if its category is not 'employee', so held employee payees (a valid category per directory.py) have their NPI purged while a legal hold applies. That breaks 'never while a legal hold applies'.
The change departs from RET-1, but the exception register has no entry for RET-1 or payments.retention (only SES-1, LOG-1 and a withdrawn MFA-1), so the deviation is not covered.
Ticket CHG-25108 is approved by Grace Kim (change_manager) at 2026-10-15T02:59Z, before the change was opened at 23:59Z, and its components list payments.retention, the only component touched.
code_review approval from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, a change_approver for payments, who is a different person from the author Linh Nguyen according to the directory.
The approval names head commit a2e976b, the only commit in the change.

The recorded CI run on head a2e976b succeeded: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skips, including the RET-1 control test test_sampled_purge_respects_hold. That test is labelled 'sample' and only uses vendor payees, so it does not exercise the changed branch. I could not re-run the suite because pytest is not installed in the review environment.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers retention.py or the other RET-1 scope paths, so no prior evidence lapses because of this change.

summary: PR-1966 changes the payments retention job so that payees in the 'employee' category are purged even while on legal hold. This directly breaks RET-1 (NPI must never be purged while a legal hold applies), and no approved exception covers it. The ticket, independent approval and CI records are in order, but CI passes only because the sample RET-1 control test uses vendor payees and never reaches the new branch. The change must be rejected.
